plan.contextChunk: This figure is a left-to-right pipeline diagram of a convolutional network, drawn with pink parallelograms for activations and blue ones for filters, strung together by black arrows. At the left, under the heading "Input," three pink sheets are stacked in oblique view and tagged R, G, and B down the left side, with W and H marking the two in-plane edges and a vertical bracket at the right reading "3 channels." An arrow leads to the middle group, headed "Layer 1 feature maps," a taller stack of five pink sheets whose edges are marked W/2 and H/2 beside a bracket reading "5 channels." A dashed line drops from the first arrow to a curly brace gathering "layer 1 filters": five groups of three small blue sheets, the leftmost tagged R, G, B and dimensioned 3 by 3. A second dashed line drops from the following arrow to a brace over "layer 2 filters," groups of five blue sheets also marked 3 and 3, with an ellipsis for the omitted groups. An ellipsis in the main arrow leads to "Logits," a vertical column of small pink diamonds beside a bracket reading "K channels" and edge marks 1 and 1, and a last arrow, labeled argmax by a dashed leader, produces the monospace word "heron." Reading sheet count against sheet size across the stages exposes the steady trade of spatial resolution for channel depth as the signal advances.

interactions.label: Step through the network
interactions.teaches: Each stage trades spatial resolution for channel depth: W×H×3 becomes W/2×H/2×5 and finally 1×1×K, so the tensor gets thinner in space and taller in channels as it advances.

interactions.label: Highlight output channel of layer 1
interactions.teaches: One pink layer-1 feature map is produced by one blue filter group — a stack of three 3×3 kernels, one per RGB input channel — so output channel count equals filter-group count.

interactions.label: Emphasize
interactions.teaches: Pink stacks are per-image activations that shrink spatially, while blue stacks are the fixed learned 3×3 weights whose depth must match the incoming channel count.

demo_steps.title: RGB input
demo_steps.narration: The input is three full-resolution pink sheets, W × H × 3, labeled R, G and B; the bracket on the right counts the 3 channels.

demo_steps.title: Layer 1 convolution
demo_steps.narration: Five filter groups, each three 3×3 blue kernels deep, sweep the input and produce five half-size pink feature maps: W/2 × H/2 × 5.

demo_steps.title: Deeper layers to logits
demo_steps.narration: Layer 2 filters are five sheets deep to match the five incoming channels; after the omitted layers the tensor has collapsed to a 1 × 1 × K column of logits.

demo_steps.title: argmax → heron
demo_steps.narration: Taking the argmax over the K logits selects the single class label, 'heron'.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: overall diagram spans about x ∈ [-13, +13], y ∈ [-7, +5]. All sheets are thin flat plates lying in the XZ plane (horizontal), drawn in an isometric pose so each reads as a rhombus with its two in-plane edges receding left-down (W) and right-down (H); stacking is along +Y. INPUT (center x=-9.5, y=+2): 3 plates, each 3.0 (W, along -X/-Z diagonal) × 3.0 (H) × 0.08 thick, vertical gap 0.55, each successive plate shifted slightly so all three read separately; R top, G middle, B bottom. LAYER 1 (center x=-0.5, y=+2): 5 plates each 1.5 × 1.5 × 0.08, vertical gap 0.45 — half the in-plane size but a taller stack. LOGITS (center x=+8.5, y=+2): 9 diamonds each 0.32 × 0.32, vertical gap 0.38, forming a narrow column; 'heron' in monospace at x=+12.3, same y as the main arrow. Main arrow chain runs at y=+2.0 horizontally: arrow -6.8→-4.4, arrow +2.0→+4.0, ellipsis '...' at x=+4.8, arrow +5.6→+7.4, final arrow +9.6→+11.4. LAYER 1 FILTERS (row centered y=-3.5, x from -12 to -4.5): 5 groups spaced 1.9 apart, each group 3 blue plates of 0.75 × 0.75 × 0.06 with vertical gap 0.35; leftmost group carries R/G/B labels and '3','3' edge labels. LAYER 2 FILTERS (row centered y=-3.5, x from +1.5 to +6.5): two drawn groups of 5 blue plates each (0.75 × 0.75, gap 0.35) with '...' between them at x=+4. Curly braces sit above each filter row (y≈-1.6) spanning its width, captions 'layer 1 filters' / 'layer 2 filters' under horizontal rules at y≈-6.3. Dashed bezier leaders run from arrow-1 midpoint (-5.6, +2) down to the layer-1 brace apex (-8.2, -1.5), and from arrow-2 midpoint (+3.0, +2) down to the layer-2 brace apex (+4.0, -1.5). Vertical channel brackets: at x=-7.4 for '3 channels', x=+1.2 for '5 channels', x=+9.6 for 'K channels', each a thin vertical line with end caps spanning the stack height, label rotated 90°. Palette: activation pink fill #F9D3D2 (highlight #F2A8A3), filter blue fill #BFE3F2 (highlight #7FC8E8), all outlines black #000 at ~2px, text black serif, 'heron' monospace, background white. Dimmed (non-emphasized) elements drop to ~25% opacity / light gray outline.
interactionPlan.notes: Build every sheet as a thin BoxGeometry or an extruded rhombus with a black EdgesGeometry / LineSegments overlay to reproduce the heavy ink outline; use an OrthographicCamera in a fixed isometric pose (no user orbit) so the parallelogram silhouettes match the source exactly. Render all text (titles, R/G/B, W, H, W/2, H/2, channel brackets, captions, 'heron', 'argmax') as CSS2DObject HTML labels so fonts stay crisp and rotated bracket labels are easy. Arrows: Line + cone mesh, or Line2 with a triangle sprite head. Dashed leaders and curly braces: THREE.Line with LineDashedMaterial along a CatmullRomCurve3 sampled in the screen plane (z=0). Draw order matters for the stacks — sort plates back-to-front so the higher sheets overlap correctly; a slight per-plate XZ offset (0.1 units) reproduces the staggered look. Highlighting is done by lerping material color/opacity, not by moving geometry, except for the channel slider which may lift the selected pink plate and its blue filter group by ~0.2 units. Keep all animation transitions ~300ms eased.

interplay between feature maps and filter banks in a CNN:

The interplay between feature maps and filters banks in a CNN. You can think of the input image itself as an R, G, B feature map and the output logits as a 1x1 resolution feature map with class logits as the channels.

discrepancies: Default state (stage = 'input') fades ~75% of the diagram to near-white with label opacity 0.16, so at first glance the figure does not read as the full source pipeline — the layer-1 maps, logits, and both filter banks are ghosted out rather than drawn in their source pink/blue.

The whole composition occupies only a small central fraction of the canvas (roughly 500×200 px of a 1066×768 viewport), leaving large empty margins; the source fills its frame edge-to-edge, and the reduced scale makes the small logit diamonds and '3'/'1' dimension labels hard to read.

Rotation is disabled (controls.enableRotate = false), so the isometric plates behave as a fixed poster; the box thickness that would show the plates are volumetric is barely perceptible at this zoom, unlike the strongly drawn heavy-ink stacked sheets in the source.

The rotated bracket labels ('3 channels', '5 channels', 'K channels') sit very close to / over their bracket lines and are noticeably smaller (14px) relative to the tiny drawing, whereas in the source they are the same weight as other annotations.
evaluation.notes: Layout, element counts (3 input planes, 5 half-size feature maps, 5×3 and 5-deep filter groups, 9 logits), arrows, braces, brackets and all major labels faithfully reproduce the source with an excellent set of stage/channel/focus/demo interactions; main weaknesses are the heavily dimmed default state and the small on-canvas scale that undercut first-glance recognizability.
action_items: Make the default state show the complete diagram (e.g. start at the final stage or add an 'all' option) so the initial view matches the source before the user steps through stages; alternatively reduce the dim factor from 0.80/0.16 to something like 0.45/0.5 so hidden stages remain legible.

Increase heightFraction / tighten the camera framing so the diagram fills the canvas width instead of occupying a small central patch, which will also make the logit diamonds and '3'/'1' dimension labels legible.
Bump the rotated channel-bracket labels to match the other annotation labels' size and offset them further from the bracket line to avoid visual collision.
Re-enable OrbitControls rotation (or add a small 'tilt' toggle) so the plate thickness and stacking depth of each tensor can actually be seen in 3D.

feedback.rationale: The concept and element decomposition are faithful and complete; the remaining issues are implementation details (default dim state, camera framing/scale, label sizing, disabled rotation) that the generator can fix directly.

discrepancies: Default state highlights layer-1 feature map 1 and filter group 1 in a darker pink/blue (channel slider at 1); the source shows all plates in the same uniform pastel fill, so the opening view is slightly off-model.

The curly braces beneath the filter banks are rendered as very shallow, thin arcs barely distinguishable from a straight line, whereas the source shows pronounced curly braces with a clear central apex meeting the dashed leader.
Blue filter groups are packed closer together horizontally (and the layer-2 groups sit closer to the ellipsis) than in the source, where each 3×3×3 group is clearly separated with more whitespace.

Vertical gaps between the plates in the layer-1 feature-map stack (and the input RGB stack) are larger relative to plate size than in the source, making the stacks look taller/airier than the tightly stacked originals.

Tighten the vertical plate spacing in the input and layer-1 stacks and widen the horizontal gaps between blue filter groups to match the source proportions.
